kitDescription: Sin: Swift Bunny is a Water sniper-rifle Attacker who permanently buffs her own ATK by 15.35% and, on every full-charge shot with her base rifle, briefly doubles that shot's normal-attack damage and adds 52.12% charge damage for one round. She operates in one of two 'Bunny Mode' states: Stance gives her a large permanent critical rate and critical damage boost, while Engage instead converts her normal attacks (and her special weapon) to true damage; she starts the fight in Stance and can only switch by deliberately holding a full charge for a second, so in practice a fight is played in one mode. Her Burst Skill raises her own ATK by 110% for 5 seconds, hits all enemies for 516.6% of final ATK, and adds a mode-dependent follow-up nuke: 958.9% plain damage in Stance or 854.6% true damage in Engage. Casting her burst also swaps her to the 'Swift Piercing' weapon for 5 seconds — a fast 0.5-second fixed-charge rifle dealing 73.22% per shot with a 300% full-charge multiplier. Mode entry also drags any Bunny-Mode teammates into her mode, which only matters on teams with another Bunny unit.

skill1.explanation: Driver test pins one grant at frame 0, targetSlug self, expiresFrame null. battleStart vs passive is cosmetic for a permanent frame-0 buff.

verdictRationale: No real gotchas. The S6 blind override is block-equivalent to the shipped one (differences: passive vs battleStart on the frame-0 ATK, stage:3 on a Burst III burstCast, mode label strings, and the blind's maxAmmo 10 vs the driver's engine-refill reading of the kit-silent swap magazine — both ⚑-flagged with the same footage recipe). The mechanical convergence check is GREEN: the verbatim S5 file wires onEvent at the CompOptions top level where runComp never reads it (cfg.onEvent is the harness path, as the driver's own passing test demonstrates), so verbatim it captures zero events — a blind-harness RECON error, not a model divergence; with only that one-line wiring routed through cfg, all 20 runnable blind assertions pass against the shipped override with its 5 declared GAP skips. Every shared-prior trap both S2b reviewers pre-registered is closed by a discriminating counterfactual in the driver's 21-green test file: durationShots-not-seconds, normalAttackPct-not-attackDamagePct, swapGate off during Swift Piercing, burstCast-not-fullBurstEnter (real in the dual-B3 fixture), Stance-default mutual exclusion of the mode packages and burst riders, no Pierce from the name. Discrimination holds — each load-bearing assertion has a named nearest-wrong patch that flips it. Same-model residuals for the owner to spot-check: (1) all five agents share the static-Stance-default convention, so real play's mode duty cycle (and the ~1s Engage opening-hold cost) is untested — grade both modes as a pair per the caveat; (2) the swap shot economy (driver ≈9 rounds via engine refill vs blind's 10) directly scales the whole swap contribution and awaits the footage count; (3) the theme-21 one-round boundary phase is pinned to the convention, not to a popup read.
